scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge that occurred 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Haruto Tanaka and I'm 43. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Haruto, thank you for reaching out. I understand the frustration of seeing an unexpected charge after returning from your travels. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the transaction ID for the charge in question?
Sure, my email is h.tanaka@email.com and the transaction ID is TXN-9982734.

Thank you, Haruto. I have successfully located your account and verified the transaction. According to our 'Service Billing Policy 4.2', refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the transaction date. However, since you are only four days past the window and have been a loyal customer for over two years, I can request a one-time exception for you.
That would be incredibly helpful, thank you so much for understanding.

You are very welcome. I have submitted the request for the refund of $49.99 to your original payment method. You should see the funds reflected in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank's processing time. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that covers everything. Thank you for your help!
It was my pleasure, Haruto. Thank you for being a valued customer, and I hope you have a great rest of your day.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the account and transaction, acknowledged the policy violation, and utilized a one-time customer loyalty exception to process the full refund.

judge_scores.justification: The agent efficiently verified the account using appropriate details, demonstrated strong empathy by acknowledging the customer's travel situation, and clearly cited 'Service Billing Policy 4.2' before applying a valid loyalty exception to process the refund. The entire interaction was handled smoothly within the agent's authority without any unnecessary friction or delay.
